scope.full_decode_and_timestamps: All 6804 encoded frames across all 12 normal/slow MP4s, independently checked by validate_motion_comparison.py.
scope.visual_method: Ordered contact sheets of every independently rendered after-pose at source 60Hz, in front/side/three-quarter views; selected old matching views and earlier full old-gait review for comparison.
scope.normal_and_slow: Both encodings use the same inspected source poses; normal time is 60 source poses/second, slow is 30 source poses/second duplicated to output 60fps. Rhythm/hold assessment combines ordered poses with exact timestamps and trajectory derivatives.
scope.not_in_this_review: Godot runtime capture, terrain IK and player control are reviewed in separate runtime reports.

observations.result: The period is 1.05s rather than .9s, at the same 1.4m/s. The 73.5cm step is carried by forward/rear leg travel; ordered side poses show heel-rise and passing rather than the whole body waiting for the swing foot. Support knees extend through midstance. Front and diagonal views retain narrow noncrossing ankle paths.

No repeated nonterminal Action frames or whole-pose hold was visible in the ordered 60Hz samples. Arm reversals naturally slow near their extrema, while feet and knees continue. Authored joins independently pass position/velocity/acceleration limit checks; timestamps are exactly 1/60s across video joins.

The rear elbow now passes behind the torso and the hand returns beside the waist. Chest-relative upper-arm motion is about -38 to +20 degrees, and elbow flexion changes about 80 to 105 degrees. The arms stay near the sides without being pinned there. Frontal and diagonal views show alternating arm/leg coordination and thorax response rather than a fixed bent-arm frame.

Ordered side views show compliant knee loading, heel recovery, toe-off and flight. The pelvis has one rise/fall pair per step, replacing the old double pulse. The foot does not remain flat throughout support. No new body jump, backwards knee branch or obvious hand/body intersection was seen in these full-body source views.

The source numerical comparison separates sampled FK velocity changes from mathematical curve continuity. Walk knee peak adjacent velocity change falls from about 1.867 to .978m/s; Jog knee from about 4.598 to 1.517m/s. The nonzero remaining values represent finite 60Hz acceleration and are not reported as perfectly zero motion.

followup: All 15 derived-motion GIFs and Godot execution require the separate final artifact/runtime review before release.
